source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #302 (branch fix/189-tos-register-study at head 1cdd6778f371f6639d7849cc715ba36c8a09527d — the TOS-in-register dispatch study for #189: docs/core/tos-register-study.md plus the standalone prototype tools/tos-register-prototype.rs, moved out of docs/ by the Codex fix commit 1cdd677; no library or binary code changes; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45454071608 and 45454083553 against the branch and pull-request run 45441631498, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #302 (#189, TOS-in-register dispatch study). This PR changes no code that is linked into any embedder configuration: it adds the study document docs/core/tos-register-study.md and the standalone prototype tools/tos-register-prototype.rs (a single-file rustc program, not a Cargo target). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45454023404, 45454038378 and 45454054158 on main at 04bca9a8222d11a3d8db61204440e3d74a37c949): unmodified main produces byte-identical sizes to this branch on all 32 gated series and fails the gate on the same two series, so the delta is entirely main-side baseline staleness, not this PR. The checked-in baseline was measured on the PR #300 branch tree (3421c44: main 93581e8 plus PR #300) before PR #299 (precompiled-module codec, #196) merged; on the merged main (04bca9a) 26 of the 32 gated series differ from that baseline. Most library configurations shrink (in release, stripped file -1,000 B in core to -1,896 B in wasi, stripped .text -1,056 B to -1,952 B; in release-size, stripped file -32 B to -128 B and stripped .text -16 B to -80 B where they change); the baseline configuration is unchanged in both profiles. Only two series grow, each by 16 B: release-size core stripped .text (787,111 B to 787,127 B) and release-size wasi-threads stripped file (1,940,824 B to 1,940,840 B) — these two are the gate failures. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is now the release core-nosimd stripped file series at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,792 B), followed by the release component stripped file series at +9.77% (2,433,656 B to 2,671,528 B); both are slightly below the PR #300 cumulative figures because the merged main shrank against the PR #300 branch tree. The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples.
